content: {"rules": ["Forecast models tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices fall sharply after peak forecasts.", "Sentiment spikes near 1.00 often precede price corrections, indicating overbought conditions that trigger downward momentum.", "Model forecasts consistently lag true price movements by 3–5 days, suggesting delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.", "High sentiment positivity (≥0.67) correlates with forecast overshoots, especially in the first 10 days of the 30-day window.", "Price corrections after forecast peaks are more pronounced when sentiment is neutral or negative, indicating sentiment-driven volatility.", "Models exhibit persistent bias toward higher prices when recent history shows downward trends, suggesting failure to capture mean-reversion signals.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment history includes multiple negative readings, indicating model calibration to bearish sentiment.", "True price movements often diverge from forecasts after day 15, suggesting models underfit long-term trend reversals."] }
